layers.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / background plate reconstruction. From the supplied approved El Unicornio motorcycle illustration, create ONLY the empty DESERT HIGHWAY BACKGROUND layer for the same card. Return one fully opaque full-bleed image at exactly the same 1024 x 1536 portrait canvas and registration. Keep the existing background's horizon, perspective, sweeping road, visible sky/clouds, left and right sandstone mesas, distant mountains, scattered cacti, desert colors and rich faceted illustration style precisely where they already are. Do not change the camera or recompose the landscape.

REMOVE THE ENTIRE UNICORN AND ENTIRE MOTORCYCLE: no character, horn, helmet, mane, sunglasses, jacket, sweater, arms, hands, yellow trousers, boots, wheels, front forks, handlebars, headlight, indicators, engine, exhaust or any trace of motorcycle. REMOVE THE LARGE RED-ORANGE FOREGROUND ROCK IN THE BOTTOM LEFT and its attached prominent grass blades along the very bottom edge; that rock and its grass have their own separate foreground layer. Reconstruct all regions previously hidden by the character, bike and corner rock with a seamless natural continuation of the desert highway and landscape. Fill the top and upper-middle hidden areas with matching sky and distant mesas according to the existing horizon. Fill the lower hidden areas with the sweeping warm asphalt and a little roadside shoulder, obeying the road's original turn and vanishing point. Keep road markings coherent, with no arbitrary diagonal lines, no holes and no vaguely motorcycle-shaped shadows or silhouettes. The previously hidden road should be complete and convincing even with both other layers switched off. This is a clean scenery plate suitable for moving the character and foreground by a few pixels during parallax.

Preserve the broad turquoise/cobalt sky, cream faceted clouds, copper-gold redrock mesas, blue-violet far mountains, warm sunset lighting and stylized angular low-poly treatment of the source. Preserve the sense of speed through restrained road streaks in the lower portion, but remove all bike-specific cast shadows and localized dust silhouettes. No nearby new props, vehicles, people, animals or oversized rocks. No title, border, text, watermark or transparency. Exact same canvas and perspective, background layer only.

Use case: background-extraction / precise-object-edit. Create the MIDDLE SUBJECT PARALLAX LAYER from image 1, the approved El Unicornio motorcycle illustration. Image 2 is the separate FRONT layer already extracted, provided ONLY to identify exactly which components must be absent from this middle layer. Deliver an actual transparent RGBA PNG at the EXACT SAME 1024 x 1536 portrait canvas. Strict registration: keep every retained part in precisely its existing image-1 position, scale, shape, angle and perspective. Do not center the cutout, enlarge it, reposition it, or crop away transparent canvas.

KEEP: the entire cheerful slightly derpy pink unicorn rider, single pearlescent horn, black chrome-edged open-face helmet, sunglasses, banded pastel rainbow mane, mint turtleneck and aqua unicorn-emblem sweater, black leather jacket, yellow pants, boots, pink hands, BOTH handlebars and grips, and the motorcycle's MAIN BODY: fuel tank, steering neck, seat, engine, frame, rear suspension, rear wheel, exhaust pipes and foot pegs. Match image 1 faithfully without redrawing his expression or changing his clothes. Keep the head and horn exactly where they were. Fill in the very small hidden portions of the main tank/frame/engine that were occluded by the front fork/headlight assembly, providing a modest natural overlap underneath the foreground when restacked. These reconstructed areas should remain a physically plausible motorcycle body, not an arbitrary flat opaque shape.

REMOVE entirely to true transparency: the front wheel/tire/rim/hub/axle, front fender, both long front fork tubes and their upper caps/clamps, round headlight and both amber front indicators—the entire front assembly visible in image 2. There must be NO front wheel, NO front forks, NO headlight and NO orange indicator lamps remaining in this middle layer. Keep the continuous handlebars in the rider's hands, however; their attachment point may be naturally visible now that the front assembly has been lifted off. Also remove the foreground bottom-left red-orange rock and attached grasses, which are on image 2. REMOVE all background: sky, clouds, mesas, cacti, road, ground, dust, golden haze, shadows on road and scenery. Do not paint a new motorcycle front wheel where the old one was removed. Empty spaces within and around the motorcycle are transparent, except authentic retained engine/frame/rear-wheel components. The lower-right region formerly occupied by the large front tire should now be almost entirely transparent.

Reproduce the same crisp faceted low-poly illustration, angular chrome and gold-lit black leather, original light direction and original colors. Clean sharply masked antialiased edges, no halo, no glow, no drop shadow, no opaque background scraps. PNG alpha zero everywhere outside retained actual objects. No fake checkerboard, colored matte, white/black background, text, labels or border. This is one registered middle layer from the original source, not a new redesigned motorcycle or pose.

Use case: background-extraction / precise-object-edit. Extract the FOREGROUND PARALLAX LAYER from this exact supplied El Unicornio motorcycle artwork. Return a genuine transparent RGBA PNG on the SAME 1024 x 1536 portrait canvas. Preserve pixel registration: every retained object must stay at precisely its existing position, scale, angle and shape. DO NOT recenter, resize, crop, recompose, rearrange or redesign any item. The transparent empty space above and around the retained objects is essential.

KEEP ONLY these foreground objects, reproducing their original intricate faceted illustration faithfully: (A) the motorcycle's COMPLETE FRONT WHEEL assembly in the lower-right: black front tire, wheel rim, hub, brake/axle hardware, the dark front fender, BOTH long chrome front fork tubes with their lower legs and upper fork clamps/caps, plus the attached round gold-lit headlamp and both small amber front signal lamps. Keep this assembly connected exactly as it appears, but EXCLUDE the handlebars and handgrips, which belong to the rider layer. The top of the retained assembly is approximately at y=600 in this 1024x1536 source; the tire ends around y=1490. Reconstruct only any tiny assembly parts hidden by objects being removed, to make clean usable contours. (B) the large orange-red faceted ROCK IN THE BOTTOM-LEFT CORNER and its attached sparse golden grass blades at the bottom edge, in their exact original locations. Keep the two object groups separate with transparent space between them. The rock should still touch the left and bottom canvas edges where it does in the source.

REMOVE everything else to alpha zero: the entire unicorn, helmet, horn, mane, sunglasses, all clothing, both arms and hands, handlebars/grips, fuel tank, engine, seat, frame, rear wheel, exhaust pipes, boots and foot pegs; ALL sky, clouds, mesas, cacti, desert, road, road markings, dust, cast shadow, and ground. Preserve true transparency through open spaces in the forks and wheel hardware and between the rock and front-wheel assembly. Keep the original chrome's reflected gold highlights as material detail, not as extra opaque background. Do not leave an opaque road-shaped region behind the wheel or forks.

This is layer extraction from the supplied art, not a new illustration. Original sharp angular low-poly facet style, original colors and golden lighting, clean antialiased edges, no outlines or added shadows. No checkerboard pattern painted into the image, no white/black/colored backdrop, no text or labels. Actual transparency throughout all empty areas. Full 1024 x 1536 canvas and original registration are mandatory.

note: Source artwork layers, not yet fitted to the repository's 1024 x 1422 printed card canvas. Keep relative subject-to-prop parallax small because the front forks must remain joined to the handlebars.
